title: Tarte à l'Oignon
subtitle: Alsatian onion tart
excerpt: Tarte à l'oignon is an Alsatian onion tart: a blind-baked shortcrust case filled with very slowly cooked sweet onions, lardons, cream, and eggs. The onions must cook for at least 45 minutes until completely soft and beginning to caramelise. Rushing them produces a filling that tastes raw and sharp.
sourceNotes: Tarte à l'oignon is a staple of Alsatian cooking, the region of France that borders Germany and Switzerland. The combination of onions, lardons, and cream in a pastry case is characteristic of the Franco-German tradition of Alsace.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze fully cooled. Defrost overnight in the fridge. Reheat at 160°C fan for 15 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The onions can be cooked up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: The filling for this tart requires patience. Start the onions on a medium-low heat and do not rush them. They need 40 to 50 minutes to soften completely, turn translucent, and begin to caramelise at the edges. Only at that point will they be sweet enough for the filling. Use six to eight medium onions: they will cook down to about a quarter of their original volume.

Melt the butter in a large wide pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions and a generous pinch of salt. Stir to coat. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring every 5 minutes, for 45 to 50 minutes until the onions are very soft and golden. They should smell sweet and caramelised.
Add the lardons and thyme for the last 10 minutes of cooking. Fry together until the lardons are cooked through. Remove from the heat and cool slightly.

Roll the pastry to 3 mm thick and line a 23 cm tart tin. Chill 30 minutes. Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Blind-bake with baking beans for 15 minutes, remove beans, bake 5 minutes more. Reduce oven to 180°C fan.
Whisk the eggs and cream together, season with black pepper. Mix with the onion and lardon mixture. Pour into the pastry case. Bake at 180°C fan for 25 to 30 minutes until set. Rest 10 minutes.

items.cause: Onions were not cooked long enough and still have a raw, harsh flavour
items.fix: The onions need a minimum of 40 minutes over low-medium heat to become truly sweet. There is no shortcut.

content.text: Alsace sits on the Rhine between France and Germany. The tarte à l'oignon is related to the Zwiebelkuchen (onion cake) eaten across the Rhine in Baden-Württemberg during the new wine season in autumn. In Alsace, the dish is eaten year-round as part of the region's tradition of generous, filling cooking.
